banner.title: THE HONOR OPENER AND TABLE 41, printed capture pp. 69-70 - the OA honor round

No contested cells detected within the single source: the T41 rows are five fixed base honors plus the single die-roll row (the yakuza 1d20 + 20 read pins as the 21-40 bounds; the class row order pins as the 0-6 code: shukenja, sohei, kensai, bushi, hengeyokai, wu jen, yakuza). The T41 base-honor column pins as the lo and hi bounds. OCR normalization: none required for this range beyond the yakuza die read - the honor opener prose carries the printed em dashes. The Altering Family Honor and Effects of Honor prose and Table 42 (capture pp. 70-72) are deliberately left for the next rounds

consts.name: dguHonorMax
consts.comment: Gaining and losing prose (capture p. 70): no character can have more than 100 points of honor

bools.name: dguHonorReflectsFamily
bools.comment: Honor opener prose (capture pp. 69-70): honor reflects the character and the character of his family - the family affects the character and vice versa

bools.name: dguHonorBringsRespect
bools.comment: Honor opener prose (capture pp. 69-70): with honor comes respect, power, influence and position; without it, disrespect, humiliation and insults

bools.name: dguHonorEasierToLose
bools.comment: Honor opener prose (capture pp. 69-70): honor is easier to lose than to gain

bools.name: dguDishonorDeeds
bools.comment: Honor opener prose (capture pp. 69-70): breaking faith, treachery, cowardice and unavenged insults cause a loss of honor

bools.name: dguHonorDeeds
bools.comment: Honor opener prose (capture pp. 69-70): valiant deeds, self-sacrifice, mastery of skills and keeping faith earn honor

bools.name: dguHonorImprovesReactions
bools.comment: Honor opener prose (capture pp. 69-70): gaining honor brings better encounter reactions, gifts and better replacement characters

bools.name: dguHonorNotAlignment
bools.comment: Honor opener prose (capture pp. 69-70): oriental honor is not a judgment of good and evil - a cruel villain can hold high honor and a heroic samurai low honor

bools.name: dguHonorDeedsBoth
bools.comment: Honor opener prose (capture pp. 69-70): honor measures the deeds of the character and the family clan - obedience, loyalty, talent and success, regardless of alignment

bools.name: dguHonorPointsTracked
bools.comment: Honor points prose (capture pp. 69-70): players record honor points - the DM gives them at the end of an adventure or major encounter and takes them away for dishonorable actions

bools.name: dguNotEveryAdventure
bools.comment: Honor points prose (capture pp. 69-70): characters do not earn honor points for every adventure - they must do something special

bools.name: dguClanStartByBirthRank
bools.comment: Starting honor prose (capture p. 70): family-clan characters start with the base honor determined by birth rank, adjusted by the Table 39 results - the family honor

bools.name: dguFamilyHonorFloorZero
bools.comment: Starting honor prose (capture p. 70): a negative family honor is raised to 0

bools.name: dguClanStartAddsBirthrights
bools.comment: Starting honor prose (capture p. 70): the starting honor is the family honor plus the birthright bonuses plus the character's lowest ability score

bools.name: dguNoClanT41Base
bools.comment: Starting honor prose (capture p. 70): characters without family clans take the Table 41 base honor by class or race, plus the lowest ability score

bools.name: dguClassSensitivity
bools.comment: Gaining and losing prose (capture p. 70): classes gain and lose honor at different rates - a samurai's honor fluctuates more than a wu jen's or shukenja's

bools.name: dguDmAwardsHonor
bools.comment: Gaining and losing prose (capture p. 70): honor points are always awarded by the DM, normally at the end of an adventure; the DM's judgment is final; the typical awards are listed on Table 42

bools.name: dguDmJudgment
bools.comment: Gaining and losing prose (capture p. 70): the list cannot cover every situation - the DM relies on his judgment using the table as a guideline
